pass_a_gloss: We who are from the nations say concerning ourselves, repenting of the false things we thought were true: 'Indeed, the hills and the strength of the mountains were vanity'; but concerning Israel who is to be saved among us: 'Nevertheless, by the Lord our God is the salvation of the house of Israel.' Whether confessing our sins, in which our fathers also were involved and we ourselves were idolaters, we say: 'The shame has consumed the labors of our fathers from their youth, their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.' 'The shame has consumed the labors of our fathers,' and these things said. Therefore, if the wicked labor of the fathers and the false work of the fathers is to be consumed, shame must arise; for before shame, the labor of the fathers is not consumed < and what follows. Therefore, let us consider the differences among those who sin. There are those who sin and are not ashamed nor do they feel shame for their sins nor do they blush. Such are those who have become calloused and have given themselves over to every licentiousness and every impurity. For the nations, in what way, as excellence, do they at times recount their fornications and adulteries, not even ashamed to confess having done such things, nor do they call them sins. As long as they are not ashamed, their labors are not consumed; their sins are not consumed. The beginning of good things is to be made to feel shame for something one did not feel shame for. Therefore, I do not consider it a curse when the prophets say: 'Let them be ashamed and let them be confounded, all who hate Zion.' For they pray that the insensible to the works of shame may come to feeling, so that, being ashamed, they may be able to consume their labors and their sins.
